messages:
mara: kicking off a focused PRD/RFC thread for an initiative: adaptive kernel routing + seq-aware KV eviction. customer ask: AtlasPay wants p99 latency reduction for typical 4k-8k flows but cannot accept >25% cost increase. attaching proposal in thread — please read and react.

ken: quick ask — can we get concrete acceptance criteria? p99, cost delta, and safety rollback triggers.

sachin: +1. runtime note: kernel selection depends on sequence distribution. proposal's heuristic (seq < 512 -> fast-attn, otherwise kv-attn) might be too coarse for multi-turn sessions. need a lighter-weight classifier. also, switching kernels can change FP outputs; we need a regression harness.

elaine: from product/observer POV: we need per-kernel p50/p95/p99, per-route token cost, and a simple "regret" metric: fraction of switched requests where response length or top token differs beyond threshold. dashboard wireframes incoming.

mara: proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- p99 tail (user-observed) on target workload decreases by >= 15% compared to baseline.
- end-to-end token cost per 1k requests increases by <= 25%.
- regression harness shows < 0.5% semantic divergence on eval prompt set.
- automatic rollback triggers if p99 increases > 10% from canary baseline or error rate > 0.5%.

ken: edge cases to call out: batching interactions when mixing kernels (per-batch kernel homogeneity?), KV cache TTL mismatch across variants, and the case where fallback kernel can't resume KV state -> huge latency spike. propose explicit requirement: a kernel must be able to accept warm KV snapshots in <50ms.

sachin: rollout plan suggestion (runtime-friendly):
1) local unit canary: run kernel selection logic in simulation on production traces for 48h.
2) 1% traffic canary for 6h with detailed traces. smoke checks: p50/p95/p99, token cost, system CPU/GPU utilization.
3) 5% 24h, 20% 48h, then full. automated rollback at each stage.

mara: ops/infra asks: what's the capacity delta? will we need extra instances for mixed-kernel capacity? also we need a cost-safety cap enforceable by routing (stop ramp if cost per token > X).

ken: likely need +10% GPU headroom during ramps. we can enable kernel affinity to avoid mixing in same instance where it hurts scheduling.

elaine: acceptance tests to include: prompt anchor suite (20 prompts covering long-range, short-range, instruction-following), plus an adversarial set for hallucination checks. layout: run pre/post diffs and present sample counterfactuals.

ops-bot: deploy checklist created: `rfc/adaptive-kernel/deploy-checks.md` linked. prerequisites: alerting, dashboards, canary routing, and rollback playbook.

deploy-bot: canary pipeline ready if owners assigned.

mara: owners so far: mara (product), ken (eng runtime), sachin (kernel infra), elaine (observability). target for initial canary: two weeks.

ken: quick implementation note: we'll add a `kernel_score` in request metadata and a cheap classifier in front of dispatcher. also around KV eviction: propose TTL = 30m for hot prefixes, but evict by LRU+seq-awareness if memory pressure > 80%. need explicit config knobs.

sachin: edge-case: bursty very long sequences that oscillate kernel choice mid-request. requirement: kernel choice must be stable for lifetime of request once started, and preflight check must pick based on predicted final length (best-effort).

mara: agreed. I'll update the PRD with these criteria and a short rollout timeline + owners. please drop quick comments or thumbs within 48h so we can lock scope for the sprint. :thumbsup:

ken: reading now, will add inline notes.

sachin: I'll run the 48h simulation on the Monday trace dump and post results.

elaine: I'll sketch dashboards and the eval set by EOD tomorrow.

ops-bot: reminder: next runtime sync on Tue 10:30 — add this to agenda.
